Docs / Concepts

Knowledge and learning

ATL retains source-backed claims, context, and lessons locally. Learning means recorded knowledge and bounded policy calibration; it does not retrain provider model weights.

Inspect and recall

Open Knowledge and inspect a claim's source and revision before reuse.

atl memory status
atl memory recall "queue recovery"

Read the CLI reference before adding or forgetting memory. Preserve failed attempts as well as successes.

Trace evidence

Brain stores sources, immutable raw snapshots, claims, events, and context packs under .trust/manager/brain/. Remembered claims do not bypass task checks. See resource model.

Learn from execution

Execution records preserve configured provider/model, sessions, and observed usage. Resource calibration uses qualifying verified history within configured limits. Missing tokens stay unknown. See execution reports for eligibility, sample minimums, and anti-self-training rules.

Record a useful lesson

Include the original condition, action, output/failure, remedy, verification result, and reusable scope. Avoid secrets and universal conclusions from one fixture. The mock report records failures and accomplishments separately. Review research before promotion through research and navigation.

Source: runtime/lib/brain.mjs, memory.mjs, execution-report.mjs, resource-policy.mjs. Locate corresponding verifiers in the catalog.
